articles.title: Palestinians gained 'nothing' from October 7, Egyptian businessman Naguib Sawiris says
articles.description: In an interview with FRANCE 24, Egyptian businessman Naguib Sawiris called the October 7 attacks a "horrible act of terrorism" that brought Palestinians "only destruction", while warning of an "expansionist" Israeli government. He also said that the economic fallout from the Iran war is already "happening", defended doubling his UAE investment despite the regional conflict, and praised Syria's new president.

articles.title: Le prix Nobel de littérature 2026 décerné à la Canadienne Anne Carson
articles.description: La poétesse a été distinguée «pour son œuvre audacieuse et inventive qui, dans un dialogue ludique avec la tradition classique, a créé de nouvelles formes pour la littérature contemporaine». Elle reçoit la plus grande récompense littéraire au monde et la plus dotée de plus d’un million d’euros.

related.title: 🔴Nobel Prize in Literature awarded to Canada’s Anne Carson
related.description: The Nobel Prize in Literature was awarded to Canadian poet and essayist Anne Carson on Thursday by the Swedish Academy in Stockholm. Toronto-born Carson, 76, draws from ancient Greek and Roman literature for her works blending elements of poetry, essay and fiction. She will receive 12 million Swedish kronor (about $1.2 million) alongside the prestigious award.

articles.title: El Nino to intensify with peak in December, UN warns
articles.description: El Nino will intensify even more before peaking in December, the United Nations said Thursday, warning it could be among the strongest witnessed since at least 1950. The naturally occurring weather phenomenon is set to bring higher temperatures to much of the planet, the UN's weather and climate agency said, with its impact compounding the effects of man-made climate change.

articles.title: Eritrean troops reportedly enter Ethiopia’s Tigray region
articles.description: Eritrean troops have deployed in Ethiopia's northern Tigray region, multiple sources said Wednesday, threatening to turn an internal conflict into a wider regional war. Fighting broke out between the rebel Tigray People's Liberation Front (TPLF) and Ethiopian federal forces on September 23, sparking fears of a return to the devastating 2020-2022 civil war. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing the rebels, and the two neighbours severed diplomatic ties last week.

articles.title: Dozens killed in Russian strike on buses in Ukraine's Kramatorsk as Kyiv targets data centre
articles.description: At least 30 people were killed in a Russian strike on two buses in the Ukrainian city of Kramatorsk in the eastern Donetsk region on Thursday. Earlier, a drone hit a data centre belonging to Russian technology company Yandex, causing a fire.

articles.title: African Union launches continent's first credit rating agency
articles.description: The African Union launched the continent's first credit rating agency on Wednesday, seeking to provide an alternative to the "big three" global ratings agencies as debt burdens weigh on many African economies. The Africa Credit Rating Agency (AfCRA) — the creation of which African leaders endorsed in 2018 — was ​launched at a ceremony ‌attended by African officials in Port Louis, the capital of Mauritius, where it will be based.

articles.title: French astronaut Adenot begins journey back to Earth
articles.description: French astronaut Sophie Adenot along with the rest of the SpaceX Crew-12 has begun its journey back to earth from the International Space Station. The seasoned helicopter pilot was only the second French woman to travel to space and has now broken the record for the longest continuous stay in orbit by a European astronaut. Her splashdown is scheduled for Thursday off the coast of California.

articles.title: Strait of Hormuz crisis fuels Cairo's plastic recycling business
articles.description: In the heart of the Egyptian capital Cairo, within the labyrinthine streets of the Manshiyet Nasser district, nearly 120,000 residents process a third of the megacity's waste every day. Long marginalised, these informal recycling specialists are now undergoing a dramatic transformation due to geopolitical tensions in the Strait of Hormuz, through which polyethylene from the Gulf usually passes.

articles.title: "Cela fait cinq ans qu'il a disparu et pourtant il est là" : une grande exposition à la Cinémathèque pour rendre hommage à Jean-Paul Belmondo
